MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 26, 2019

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Raths at 5:00 p.m., on February 26, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 21, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiator Government Code Section 54956.8. The
  unimproved real property commonly referred to as “Site C” (City Housing Element)
  located on City-owned land directly adjacent to and southeasterly of the City’s Animal
  Service Center off Center Drive, and easterly of Saddleback College (Assessor Parcel
  No. 740-112-03). Agency Negotiators Dennis Wilberg, City Manager, Keith Rattay,
  Assistant City Manager & Director of Public Services, Cheryl Dyas, Director of
  Administrative Services, Elaine Lister, Director of Community Development, and
  William Curley, III, City Attorney. Negotiating Party: Mission Viejo Housing
  Authority under discussion price and terms.

City Council Minutes  1  February 26, 2019
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Raths recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council provided direction to staff in Closed Session
but no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Mayor Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Featured Businesses of the Month - INFINITI of Mission Viejo, Audi Mission Viejo
  & Volvo Cars of Mission Viejo; and S.A. Electric Inc.

  Mayor Raths presented Proclamations to Matt Gunderson and Siavosh Zadeh.

Note: This presentation was added to the agenda at the meeting.

  Recognition of Jens Nelson for his Environmental Stewardship

  Mayor Raths presented a Certificate of Appreciation to Jens Nelson.

P2.  Mission Viejo Welcomes the China National Swim Team to our Marguerite Aquatics
  Center to train

  Mayor Raths introduced the China National Swim Team and welcomed them to Mission
  Viejo.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Chris Hammer, M.V.: stated that he would like to get information to Santa Margarita Water District
customers about upcoming rate increases and he asked the City to help get the word out.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: expressed dissatisfaction with the City's handling of the California Voting
Rights Act lawsuit. She said the City Council gamed the system to maintain their seats in 2018
and the public needs to be aware that all five Council seats are up for election in 2020.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  2  February 26, 2019
 AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of February 12, 2019, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated February 1, 2019 in the Amount of $948,144.15

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated February 8, 2019 in the Amount of $858,363.03

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Second Quarter 2018/19

  Received and filed.

5.  Acceptance of Final Parcel Map 2016-114

  Approved Final Parcel Map 2016-114 and authorize the City Clerk and the City Engineer
  to sign the record map upon completion of any technical corrections required by the City
  Engineer.

6.  2018 Residential Resurfacing—Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP 19838)—
  Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

7.  Felipe Road and Olympiad Road Pavement Rehabilitation (CIP 19837)

  Approved the bid specifications, subject to minor revisions required by the City Engineer,
  and authorized staff to advertise for bids for the subject project.

8.  Interstate 5 Widening—State Route 73 to El Toro Road

  Approved Relinquishment Agreement No. 12-773 between the State Department of
  Transportation (Caltrans) and the City of Mission Viejo.

City Council Minutes  3  February 26, 2019
 NEW BUSINESS

9.  Negotiation Agreement for Site C between Mission Viejo Housing Authority and
  Brinshore Development, LLC

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to
  approve the Housing Authority Negotiation Agreement for Site C and authorize City and
  Housing Authority representatives, including the City Manager/Executive Director and his
  designated staff, along with the City Attorney, special counsel and the housing consultant
  to perform under the contract.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

10.  Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

11.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Council Member Bucknum presented the report.

12.  Orange County Veterans Advisory Council

  Mayor Raths presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

13.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum referred to public comments earlier in the meeting regarding Santa
Margarita Water District rates and the voting rights matter. She asked staff to address those issues.

City Council Minutes  4  February 26, 2019
 City Manager Wilberg noted that staff will reach out to the Water District to see if they can make
contact with the gentleman who spoke earlier and assist in getting the word out about the rate
increases. He said that the District can also present rate information at an upcoming Council
Meeting and the same can be posted on the City’s website.

City Attorney Curley stated that there is a lot going in relation to the City’s prior action on the
voting rights issue. Staff has been in contact with the Secretary of State and the Voter Education
Ad Hoc Committee has met. He said there are a lot of precedential, preliminary issues and just
because a resident doesn’t know what is going on, doesn’t mean that nothing is going on. Attorney
Curley stated that the City is well within the time frame of actions approved by opposing Council,
and the Judge and everything is going as it should be. He also said that the Council considered
very large staff reports and hosted public hearings, and the meetings were properly noticed as the
law requires. Residents did have multiple opportunities to provide input during the five-meeting
process and more than 200 members of the public responded that they were opposed to districting.
City Attorney Curley said that the attorneys that raised the CVRA issue are incredibly competent
at what they do and had the City failed, the other attorneys would have objected to the process. He
stated that everyone who knew what was going on believed the process was handled properly.

Council Member Bucknum announced that she attended the Oso Fit 5K last weekend and it was a
huge success. The event benefitted local non-profits and she thanked all those involved for a job
well done. She discussed the South Orange County Economic Coalition meeting to meet local
Congress Members and noted that Mission Viejo’s Congresswoman, Katie Porter, also held a town
hall meeting at the Norman P. Murray Community Center. Council Member Bucknum reminded
residents that Daylight Savings Time ends on March 10 and opening days for some of the baseball
leagues have been shifted due to the rain. She announced that the second annual Irish Fest will be
held on the Village Green on March 16 and she gave a shout out to the business owners who were
recognized earlier in the meeting. Council Member Bucknum said that Mission Viejo is a big city
with a small town feel and that is why she is so passionate about serving the City.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that she too attended the meeting that provided attendees the
opportunity to meet their Congressional representatives. She also attended the Drug Abuse
Prevention Coalition meeting on February 20 where Jodi Barber showed the Overtaken 2 video.
Council Member Kelley encouraged parents to look for the Overtaken videos on YouTube as they
very effectively address the opioid overdose epidemic. She reminded residents that the Drug
Prevention Coalition meetings are open to the public and are held monthly on the third Wednesday
at 6:00 p.m. Council Member Kelley discussed her attendance at the Marine Adoption
Committee’s wine tasting fundraiser and she thanked residents for coming out and
overwhelmingly supporting the event. She also thanked the San Clemente Wine Company for
providing the wine and their time.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs said he had no comments, other than to share that he just returned from his
son’s wedding in Florida.

City Council Minutes  5  February 26, 2019
 Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell announced that he attended the meeting with Congress Members and also
Katie Porter's Town Hall. He previously met with Congresswoman Porter at her office on Capitol
Hill when he was in Washington DC on a legislative advocacy trip with the Association of
California Cities-Orange County. He stated that it is good for Council Members to hear the
Congress Members’ positions so they can try to figure out how to solve some big issues in the
communities. Mayor Pro Tem Goodell announced that there is a possibility that Mission Viejo can
accept some excess soil that may come out of the freeway widening project. Although a contract
has not been awarded yet, there might be an opportunity for the City to create some more usable
space for sports programs.

Mayor Raths

14.  Appointment of City Ambassador

  Mayor Raths thanked Council Members Kelly and Bucknum for supporting him on the
  Ambassador program. He said, after talking to many people in the community, he is going
  to table the program indefinitely. Mayor Raths noted that he was hopping for unanimous
  support of the program and he doesn't like the attack that residents made on his proposed
  Ambassador, Dave Leckness.

Mayor Raths outlined his attendance at a child mental health forum hosted by Supervisor Lisa
Bartlett at Mission Hospital. The purpose was to work on ways to prevent children from getting to
the point in their lives where they don't want to live anymore. He also discussed his attendance at
additional events including the annual firefighters and law enforcement appreciation dinner at the
Elks Lodge where local first responders were honored for their valor, Congresswoman Katie
Porter’s Town Hall meeting, the Association of California Cities tour of the Orange County
Sanitation District in Fountain Valley and the Orange County Fire Authority’s Best and Bravest
annual awards dinner. Mayor Raths announced that earlier today he was at Camp Pendleton talking
with Colonel Griffin who noted that the Marine Adoption Committee has been fantastic for his
troops and they appreciate everything the City does to help the Marines.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:20 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting, in memory of Mary Young, to Tuesday, March 12, 2019, at
5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 12, 2019

City Council Minutes  6  February 26, 2019
